content.thinking:
I'm picturing the design now: a koala clinging to a vertical eucalyptus trunk mounted on a wooden base, roughly life-sized at 0.6-0.8 meters, with a side branch bearing leaves for added realism.

Actually a cleaner composition: koala sits in a fork where a horizontal branch crosses the vertical trunk, body facing forward toward camera, rear resting on the horizontal branch, one arm reaching up to grip the trunk above for support, legs dangling or gripping the branch below.

I'll settle on a clearer composition: a vertical trunk behind the koala with a horizontal branch forming a fork, the koala sitting on the branch with its back against the trunk, legs gripping forward, and one arm holding a thin leafy shoot rising in front of its chest.

I'm reconsidering the setup with a vertical trunk placed off to one side instead, so the koala sits beside it with one arm hugging the trunk while its head and body stay visible from the front, avoiding the awkward chest-blocking issue of a hug pose straight-on.

I'll thicken the horizontal branch slightly and have the hind feet curl around its front-lower edge, with toes wrapping around; thighs extend forward from the hips to knees positioned a bit higher and outward.

Actually, reconsidering the geometry: maybe the branch should run along Z instead of X, angled diagonally from the trunk, so the koala sits facing forward along the branch with hands gripping it ahead and feet tucked beneath on either side.

I'm overthinking this. Let me just settle on a simple vertical trunk with the koala clinging to it in the classic hugging pose, facing +Z toward the viewer with its head turned slightly.

Working out the exact joint coordinates now — hips, knees, and feet gripping each branch of the V, plus shoulder and hand positions reaching up to grip the limbs higher.

Rethinking proportions: crotch at y=0.5, torso 0.35, head 0.2, giving head top near 1.0. The trunk base disc sits r=0.45 at ground, with trunk radius ~0.07 up to crotch, and limbs/leaves extending to about y=1.4, so total height with foliage reaches roughly 1.45, which fits koala-scaled eucalyptus branch thickness.

Now I'm planning the skeleton for the koala as an animal rig: hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, ears, arms, legs, and digits — accounting for the koala's unique hand (two opposable thumbs plus three fingers) and foot (fused syndactyl toes plus an opposable big toe), with no functional tail. I'm also figuring out how the tree stand fits into the hierarchy, since there can only be one root joint — deciding whether to make the stand itself the root with hips as a child, or keep hips as the root per typical animal rigging conventions.

For the visual style, I'm thinking of building the koala out of blocky voxel-like boxes to get that chunky pixel-art look, choosing a texel size (around 0.02) that gives nicely proportioned chunky surfaces, and sizing the paint sheet resolution to make sure there's enough texel density across the koala's roughly 1.2 square meter surface area plus the stand.

I'll go with octagonal ngon sections for a chunky, low-poly pixel-art silhouette, combined with smooth loft for the body. Now I'm mapping out the koala's skeleton coordinates for a sitting pose—spine running from hips up through chest, neck, to head center, establishing the main proportions.

Still defining the spine chain...

Actually I'll settle on a chain "spine" with joints hips, spine1, chest parented to root, then a short neck chain leading to the head. Since koalas barely have a neck, I'll keep that chain minimal and focus on sculpting the pear-shaped body profile with the hip width around 0.34, building the sweep stations next.

I'm shaping the body as a pear silhouette with widening radii from hips to shoulders, running a spine chain that curves slightly forward from the hips up to the chest so the bum stays rounded at the base.

For the head I'm making it oversized and rounded to feel cute, with big fuzzy round ears, a protruding spoon-shaped nose, small eyes, and white cheek patches, sized proportionally larger than the body for a stylized koala look.

I'm reconsidering the head shape itself—maybe a low-poly sphere with cell-shaded fur gives a better rounded koala look than boxy pixel geometry, then I'd layer flat textured planes for the face details, making sure those decal planes are sized to match the pixel grid texel scale.

Defining the fur color palette...

I'm adding leaf clusters hanging from twig ends with small brown gumnut caps, plus a wooden base styled as a log slice disc with ring texture and bark edge, octagonal in cross-section. I'm also considering a small plaque detail, maybe with a paw-print instead of text, and scattering a bit of leaf litter on the base.

Now I'm planning the joint hierarchy: a root stand, hips as spine base, a spine chain up through chest to neck, head, jaw, and ears, with arms branching into shoulder-elbow-wrist chains ending in hands with opposable thumbs and fingers as two-joint digit chains, and legs following hip-knee-ankle chains into feet with an opposable big toe and fused toe clusters.

I'm now working out the physical layout for the base and trunk -- an octagonal slab with a beveled upper step, then the trunk rising to a crotch point where the koala's bum sits, checking that the bum radius and trunk radius don't awkwardly overlap at the given z-offsets.

If the crotch sits too low, the limb geometry ends up looking like it's piercing through the koala's body, so I'm reconsidering whether the koala should sit forward of the trunk fork instead so the limbs wrap around it naturally rather than passing through it.

Simplifying to a final layout: a vertical trunk behind the koala, with the koala perched on a horizontal branch stub extending outward to support its seated pose.

Actually, real koalas grip the branch with hind feet splayed to the sides of their bum rather than wrapping the front, so I'm adjusting the hip-knee-foot chain to splay outward and slightly forward. For the arms, I'm considering giving the koala something to hug, like a thin vertical sapling limb rising near the front of the branch, though that risks blocking the face, so I'm working out the arm placement around it.

I'm settling on a symmetrical "U"-shaped branch stand: two vertical limbs flanking the koala at roughly ±0.30 on the x-axis, joined below by the horizontal seat branch, with each arm reaching up to grip one of the uprights in a T-like pose. This naturally forms from a single trunk that forks upward into the two leaning limbs, with the koala nestled in the crotch of the V where the seat connects.

I'm reconsidering this as a man-made branch stand instead—a sculptural log with a trunk that splits into a T-shape, with a crossbar forming the seat where the koala perches, simplifying the earlier tangled limb geometry into something more structurally plausible.

Working out the U-shaped branch geometry with control points sweeping from the leaf-tipped limbs down through the seat to the trunk base, tapering the radius as it goes, then positioning the koala's bum to rest right at the seat's bottom curve.

Now I'm figuring out hip placement so the body sinks slightly into the branch, and mapping hind leg positions—hips, knees, and feet—so the legs straddle the U limb and plant naturally on its front face.

I'm working out arm placement too: shoulders, elbows, and wrists positioned so the hands can wrap and grip the limb, with fingers curling around its front.

Now placing the leaves along the limbs and twigs, with a denser cluster drooping near the top, plus a small leafy twig curving in from one limb toward the koala's mouth area for that munching detail.

For the koala itself, I'm working out the head and spine geometry: head center and radius, a spine curve running from the hips up through the chest to the base of the neck, with the head overlapping the top slightly.

Checking proportions against a real koala, my current build comes out around 0.8 m tall from bum to head top, which is too tall compared to a real sitting koala's 0.5-0.7 m height, so I need to scale the whole figure down.

Writing fur shader code...

Limbs need similar fur shading but darkening toward the extremities, with hands and feet rendered as dark charcoal paws with pinkish-grey pads, contrasting against lighter cheeks and darker forehead/ears on the head. I'm planning the paw geometry as a palm sphere with swept digit sections and cream claw spikes, anchored at the wrist joint.

For positioning, I'm figuring out where the palm sits relative to the limb's curve so the fingers wrap naturally around the forearm like a hand gripping a pole, spreading the digits along the limb's vertical axis rather than stacking them flat.

Continuing the digit curves...

I'm placing the palm pad and wrist joint connection, then working out the arm chain positions from shoulder to elbow to wrist using the limb curve path, and planning the legs so the feet and toes wrap around the lower limb at the appropriate height.

For the feet I'm defining didactyl toe pairs plus a thick clawless hallux and two smaller clawed toes, using the same wrap-path approach with slightly larger radius. For the leg IK, I'm setting up hip joints offset to the side with a bend hint pointing forward/up for the knee direction, naming the chain joints hipL/kneeL/ankleL for later preview tuning.

For fur, I'm adding ruff cards on cheeks, chest, and ear fringes using a small pixelated fuzzy tuft texture tinted by the fur color, then scattering around 120 of these tufts across the body with minimum spacing, reading the tint from the root color paint since the grayscale texture gets colorized. I'm also starting to author a sickle-shaped eucalyptus leaf as a pixel-art grid with a lighter midrib running through it.

Still writing the leaf width profile per row...

Now I'm thinking about placing leaf cards along twig frames, sizing them to feel like oversized eucalyptus leaves hanging downward with faces oriented along the flow.

I'll just use random spin around the axis for leaf variety since the preview will clarify orientation anyway, keeping triangle counts low for 400 tiny leaves. For bark texture on the limbs, I want a eucalyptus-style pattern with pale cream-grey base, orange/olive patches, and dark scribble marks painted onto the cells.

For patches and streaks, I'm using anisotropic noise sampling with elongated vertical scaling to get natural bark grain, plus random thresholds for dark scribbles and salmon-toned patches. I'm also planning small darker disc shapes for knots with a ring detail, plus short cut spikes at broken limb ends and scattered moss/lichen card patches.

Now I'm thinking through gumnuts as a tiny cluster of flattened brown spheres with lighter caps near the twig, and designing the log base as a cylinder with a flat-shaded top showing concentric ring patterns based on distance from center, switching between ring and bark coloring depending on the surface normal.

Below that I'm layering in moss patches, pebbles, flat leaf cards, and fallen gumnuts on the ground, plus considering a small plaque at the edge — maybe a pixel-art paw print or tiny "KOALA" lettering rendered as a 5x5 pixel grid.

I'm also planning the trunk and root buttresses flaring out at the base, and designing a facial decal texture for the koala's eyes, brows, pale cheek spots, muzzle, and mouth line, all built as a small pixel-art bitmap applied to the head.

Now I'm figuring out the nose shape—broad, tall, and protruding like a real koala's—deciding whether to build it as a scaled box or lathe geometry with a tiled nostril texture on its front face.

For the head, I'm going with a mix of stacked spheres and boxes for a chunky, pixel-art look: a low-poly main head sphere, cheek fluff spheres, and a pale muzzle ellipsoid, all finished with cell-shaded pixel textures. The jaw I'm planning as a separate flattened sphere or box with its own pale fur texture.

I'm working out the eyes now—considering tiny 3D parts like a dark sphere for the pupil with a small highlight cube, versus a flat pixel-texture decal on a small box. I'll likely combine spheres with highlight cubes for simplicity, then orient the head joint to aim forward.

I'm placing the head and neck joints using local-position shorthand (forward/up/left), chaining a short neck joint from the chest tip up to around (0, 0.95, 0.03), with the head joint aimed forward-up from there to form the head center near (0, 1.0, 0.05).

Now I'm laying out the spine chain through hips, spine1, and chest using an explicit path of points, then continuing the neck chain from the chest tip up to a head joint, making sure the head joint's parent and direction are set explicitly rather than relying on the chain tip naming.

For the body shape, I'm sweeping a tube along the spine chain using a radius function to define thickness, planning to layer on shoulder bumps near the chest bone to suggest muscle without overcomplicating the geometry.

Working out the radii profile along the body: tapering from wider hips at the bottom to narrower shoulders at the top, with a rounded bottom cap for the bum. I'm also offsetting the belly curve slightly forward along the normal direction to give the koala a more natural rounded torso shape following its curved spine.

Now I'm setting up the arm chains for each side, defining shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints parented to the chest, then sweeping thick radii (tapering from shoulder to wrist) to get that stocky koala-arm look, with palm spheres planned at the hand tips.

Still planning construction...

Moving to legs, I'm sweeping thigh-to-ankle radii for a tapered limb, adding a foot wedge with toes, plus rump fluff cards for texture. For the ears, I'm working out a stepped-circle pixel outline built row by row with varying half-widths to approximate a round silhouette at low resolution.

I'm giving the ear outline thickness and a darker fur tone, then layering a paler inner-ear pad with its own stepped shape plus fringe fluff cards, and deciding on the orientation so the ears face forward-sideways like a koala's.

Working out the mirrored extrude orientation...

Now I'm figuring out the ear's outward tilt vector and recomputing the normal via cross product, then working out how to position the ear relative to the head using the correct left/right convention.

I'm also settling the claws as cream spikes placed at digit tips along the chain tangent, plus noting the stand bone and brow tufts before starting to write out the full code.

Setting up the trunk sweep and limb curves...

I'll add a knob sphere at the junction and flare out five root sweeps at the base. For the U-shaped limbs, I'm varying the radius along the sweep so it's thicker near the bottom and tapers toward the ends, then extending thinner twigs upward from the limb tips toward the canopy top for the eucalyptus silhouette.

Now I'm sprouting side twigs outward and upward from several points along the limbs, thinner and bearing hanging leaves, plus a terminal twig at the tip. I'm writing a helper function that sweeps a curved path and places leaf cards along it at outward/upward-facing orientations, binding them to the nearest joint and using a few colored leaf texture variants for the cards.

Writing leaf frame logic...

With 400 leaves at 4-16 triangles each the budget stays reasonable, and bending adds just a modest segment count. Now I'm thinking through the fur tufts: grayscale texture cards colored by the paint read at the root, scattered as frames across the body surface sweep, with flow and lean values tuned so the fur lies downward naturally on a seated koala. I'm also considering whether to add a ring of fluff cards around the head for cheek detail.

Scatter cheek tufts outward on the lower head with pale cream coloring, then adding ear fringe fluff pointing outward along the ear rim using directional frames. I want pixel-correct texel sizing throughout, and need to keep the flat color palette capped at 64 entries since paints and textures don't count toward that limit. Writing imports and setup code...

Picking out fur and cream color palettes with graduated tones...

Defining more color ramps...

Finishing fur paint, then I need a separate head paint function with lighter cheeks and muzzle around the face center, darker forehead, and no strong eye markings since koalas lack distinct facial patterns. I'm also sketching the limb bark paint, base log coloring, and flat leaf colors before moving on to specific API part details.

Now I'm working out eye placement geometrically, computing where the eye spheres sit on the ellipsoid head surface using the radius equations so the eyes protrude slightly without floating off the skull.

For facial details, I'm deciding to skip decals and rely on embedded sphere parts for most features, but considering one small pixel decal under the nose for a mouth line to suggest the philtrum and muzzle.

Thinking about the muzzle, I'll make it a separate pale sphere part positioned at the head's front-lower area with the nose on top and jaw below, then insert a thin dark box between the muzzle and jaw to read as the mouth line rather than fussing with decals.

Now I'm sketching out the head's part hierarchy: a scaled sphere for the skull, cream-furred cheek puffs positioned symmetrically, and the muzzle sphere placed slightly forward and down with a proportionally large protruding nose to match real koala anatomy.

I'm figuring out the jaw joint and lower lip geometry, assigning all these head parts to the head bone with absolute model-space coordinates, and planning forehead fur tufts before moving into the nose's tile-based texture layers with a dark base, highlight, and glint palette.

Now I'm detailing the nose box stack with nostril shading and gloss pixels, then sketching out eye spheres with highlight cubes and ear rim fringe cards.

For hands, I'm sketching a reusable digit-wrapping function that builds a catmull-rom path through joint points, sweeps a tapered hexagonal cross-section along it with rounded caps, and optionally adds a claw spike at the tip.

Checking that chain names arrays align with the correct number of spans, and working out claw placement using the chain's tip frame so the spike points along the digit's tangent direction. Now figuring out how to compute the limb's center position along the body silhouette at a given height for positioning each digit's base.

Still working out joint counts...

Palm center sits near the limb, slightly overlapping for a grounded grip, with the wrist arm reaching in from the shoulder side to meet it. For legs, I'm checking foot placement against the curved limb at matching height, making sure the foot clamps naturally onto the branch without colliding with the body's width.

I'm working out hip-knee-ankle lengths for the leg IK: measuring thigh and shin segments, confirming the ankle target is close enough that the knee bends sharply, matching a sitting koala pose with a forward-up knee hint.

For the foot, I'm placing the toes so they wrap the vertical limb's surface naturally—the opposable hallux sits toward the back while the other digits curve around the front and outer edges, spaced along the foot's contact height.

I'm checking that the digit radii (around 0.013) stay proportionate to the limb radius (0.045) so the toes wrap just outside the limb surface without gaps.

Now I'm turning to the full assembly: ear fringe and tufts, plus stand details like moss, pebbles, mushrooms, gumnuts, and a nameplate. For bark texture, I'm scattering small dark knot scars across the surface, oriented flat along the normal direction using thin box shapes to mimic scribbled bark marks.

I'm budgeting the total part count — aiming for roughly 300 parts across skeleton, head, stand, and foliage, keeping well under the 1000 limit. Now I'm sketching the actual file structure, starting with the stand's root joint definition and noting some uncertainty around the exact API calls for sticks, surfaces, and frames that I'll need to verify as I go.

Working out the spine-to-head rig: planning a short spine chain, then a neck joint or chain bridging to the head, deciding whether to model the neck as its own joint or a small chain with proper parent/role assignments.

Then I'm adding smaller facial features -- a jaw joint hinged under the head, and ear joints attached to the sides of the skull with hinge roles -- before moving on to how the body skin gets swept along the spine, figuring out polygon sides and smoothing for the fur silhouette.

Arms and legs attach to the chest and hip joints with tapered tube radii, keeping shoulders tucked inside the body mesh. Now I'm sketching a small pixel pattern for ear/tail tufts, laying out rows of "w" characters to form pointed fur tips.

Writing leaf texture function...

Still shaping the sickle geometry... I'm also planning leaf color variety and adding ground clutter like fallen leaf cards lying flat near the base.

Now I'm adding moss tufts and pebbles on the base using low-poly flattened shapes with cell-shaded paint, plus a small wooden plaque with pixel-art engraved text sized to fit the box geometry cleanly.

I'll mount the plaque slanted against the base front using a tilted box backing with a plane decal carrying the pixel texture, then start sketching 3x5 letter bitmaps for the engraved text.

Finishing the bitmaps for "KOALA" and sizing a 23x9 frame with gold lettering on dark wood, then moving to a painted ring on the stand's top cylinder using distance-based coloring from a model-space point.

Now I'm shaping the trunk's second tier with a bark layer that gets vertical streaks, and setting up the twig system with Catmull-Rom paths extending from branch tips for leaf placement.

Defining branch-off logic to spawn side twigs with drooping ends, then scattering leaves along each twig and clustering extra leaves at the tips.

I'm sizing up the foliage density: aiming for around 16 twigs with 16 leaves each for a fuller canopy, plus adding small gum nuts at twig ends using tiny spheres colored dark brown with lighter caps, grouped by color for merging efficiency before writing the final mesh-building code.

input.command: cd ~/tmp-archive/sonnet-100/koalaSonnet && grep -n "sides\|smooth" src/builder.ts | head -30; grep -n "export" src/frame.ts | head; grep -n "type SweepOptions" -A40 src/*.ts | head -70
